title: Applied ML Eval Playbook: Prompt Sets, Benchmarks, Model Onboarding, Quantization & Regression Triage
author: Priya Nair
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates best practices and step-by-step procedures for: prompt set design and onboarding, benchmark definitions and automated evaluation, model onboarding into the eval-harness, quantization profile guidance, and a reproducible regression triage process. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML reviewers, and platform owners who run quality guardrails for production inference.

Scope:
- Applies to all open and internal models onboarded to Redwood Inference evaluation systems (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Covers prompt sets, metrics, automated benchmarks, quantization test profiles, and post-deployment regression triage.
- Excludes experimental research-only evaluations; those belong in the research notebooks repository.

Ownership and contacts:
- Document owner: Applied ML & Evals (applied-ml-and-evals)
- Primary owners: Priya Nair (Applied ML), Liam Chen (Eval Harness), Aisha Patel (Model Onboarding)
- Slack: #applied-ml-evals, Pager: oncall-applied-ml (for critical production regressions)
- Model registry: model-registry.redwood.internal
- Prompt set artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets

High-level process (one-line):
1) Design prompt set -> 2) Author benchmark & metrics -> 3) Run in eval-harness (baseline) -> 4) Quantize candidate models and re-evaluate -> 5) Gate + onboard -> 6) Monitor + regression triage

1) Prompt set design and onboarding
Purpose: Create reproducible, diverse prompt sets that reflect production distributions and corner cases.
Required metadata per prompt set (YAML/JSON stored with the artifact):
- prompt_set_id: short-dash-name (e.g. customer-support-clarification-v1)
- owner: team/email
- description: one-line purpose
- sources: [internal-logs, synthetic, crowdsource]
- split: train/validation/test (ratios or explicit split files)
- seed_examples: list of canonical examples (10-50)
- tags: natural-language, reasoning, code, summarization, safety
- labels_schema: reference to label schema file (if applicable)

Design guidelines:
- Size: aim for 1k-10k examples for production benchmarks; smaller focused sets (100-500) are OK for targeted regressions.
- Distribution match: sample examples to approximate production distributions (intent, length, locale).
- Edge cases: include at least 2-5% adversarial or edge-case prompts per set.
- Annotation quality: all human-labeled items must have inter-annotator agreement (Cohen's kappa) >= 0.7 where applicable.
- Redaction: strip customer-identifiable information before onboarding.

Onboarding checklist (step-by-step):
1. Create prompt set artifact and metadata in s3://redwood-evals/prompt-sets/<prompt_set_id>/
2. Run local validation: python tools/validate_prompt_set.py --path <prompt_set_path>
3. Add dataset to eval-harness catalog: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_API_TOKEN" \
   -d '{"prompt_set_id":"<id>", "s3_path":"s3://..."}' https://eval-harness.redwood.internal/api/datasets
4. Assign reviewers and schedule baseline run against the canonical baseline model (baseline tag in model registry).
5. Approve metadata and tag prompt set as stable (status: stable) after review.

2) Benchmarks and metrics
Canonical metric families (choose per task):
- Classification: accuracy, macro-F1, confusion matrix, calibration (ECE)
- Generation: ROUGE-L, BLEU (if applicable), BERTScore, answer-level Exact Match (EM)
- Retrieval/Ranking: MRR@k, NDCG@k, recall@k
- Code: pass@k, compilation rate, correctness tests
- Safety: toxicity rate, hallucination rate (task-specific)
- Token-level diagnostics: mean token logprob, perplexity, average generation length

Benchmark report items:
- Baseline model results with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals
- Quantized model results side-by-side (delta columns for accuracy, latency, cost per token)
- Latency and cost profiling: p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), estimated cost per 1M tokens
- Stability checks: per-bucket breakdowns by prompt length, tag, and locale

SLOs and guardrails (examples):
- Production quality SLO: end-to-end application task EM >= baseline_EM - 2.0 points (absolute) OR quality regression < 3% relative.
- Latency SLO for interactive chat: p95 <= 450ms for 8k context on Dedicated hosts.
- Acceptable quantization delta: degradation in primary metric <= 1.5% absolute for customer-critical tasks; otherwise require manual review.

3) Model onboarding into eval-harness
Minimum onboarding metadata required in model-registry:
- model_id (e.g. redwood-mosaic-13b-v2)
- architecture (decoder-only / encoder-decoder)
- framework (transformers, ggml, triton binary reference)
- baseline_tag (boolean if baseline for a task)
- quantization_profiles_supported (list)
- owner_team
- model_card_url

Onboarding steps:
1. Push model binaries to model artifact store and register in model-registry.redwood.internal via internal CLI: rw-model register --id <model_id> --path s3://models/...
2. Create an eval config in eval-harness: examples/eval_config/<model_id>-<prompt_set_id>.json (see example below).
3. Launch baseline run: eval-harness run --config <eval_config> --tag baseline
4. Review automated report and if metrics meet threshold, mark model as eligible for production canary.

Example eval_config (JSON snippet):
{
  "model_id": "redwood-mosaic-13b-v2",
  "prompt_set_id": "customer-support-clarification-v1",
  "metrics": ["exact_match","rouge_l","latency_p95"],
  "batch_size": 8,
  "timeout_seconds": 600
}

4) Quantization profiles and testing guidance
Purpose: Provide repeatable profiles and tests to evaluate model-size / cost tradeoffs.
Recommended profiles (names correspond to runtime profiles used by serving/runtime):
- fp16: full-precision mixed FP16 (baseline, best quality)
- q4_0: 4-bit static quantization (fast, mild degradation for many models)
- q8_0: 8-bit quantization (good latency/cost compromise)
- int8_dynamic: dynamic int8 where supported (test for stability)

Quantization evaluation checklist:
1. Run functional tests on held-out prompt sets including safety and adversarial subsets.
2. Measure primary metric delta vs fp16 baseline and verify within acceptability thresholds (see SLOs).
3. Run randomized prompt stress test (sample 10k prompts) and assert no systemic failure modes (exceptions, extremely low logprob, bad tokenization).
4. Check numerical stability by monitoring token logprob distributions and generation-length drift.
5. If delta exceeds threshold, run per-layer ablation to identify largest contributors.

Quantization artifact metadata to include: profile_name, toolchain_version, quantize_command, artifacts location. Example quantize_command: "rw-quantize --model s3://models/redwood-mosaic-13b-v2 --profile q4_0 --out s3://models-quantized/..."

5) Regression triage playbook (for detected quality regressions)
Objective: Quickly detect, reproduce, prioritize, and remediate regressions with minimal customer impact.
Trigger detection sources:
- Canary comparisons via eval-harness scheduled runs
- Production offline monitors (sampled user prompts flagged by QA rules)
- Customer-reported failures (support tickets)

Initial detection workflow (automated):
1. Alert generated when primary metric drops > configured delta (default: 3% relative) or when safety threshold exceeded.
2. Create a triage issue in JIRA with label eval-regression and link to the eval report.
3. Assign a lead responder from applied-ml-and-evals (oncall rotation) within 1 business hour.

Reproduce and scope:
1. Re-run failing eval-config in the eval-harness with --trace and --save-responses flags.
2. Run the same eval-config against the last-known-good model artifact (use registry tag last-good).
3. Produce a delta report that includes: top 20 failing prompts, metric deltas per-bucket (by tag/length), and example responses from both models.

Root cause investigation checklist (examples):
- Model change: new weights, tokenizers, or decoding defaults?
- Serving/runtime change: kernel, compiler flags, kernel selection, or kv-cache bug?
- Quantization effects: did a new quantized artifact get promoted incorrectly?
- Prompt handling/regression: preprocessing, tokenizer mismatch, special tokens.
- Data drift: input distribution changed (locale, new intents).

Mitigation playbook (prioritized):
1. Hotfix rollback: if last-good is available and meets safety checks, roll back deployment to last-good artifact and notify customers.
2. Canary throttle: reduce traffic to canary model by 90% until fix is validated.
3. Quick patch: adjust decoding settings (temp/top_p) if decoding-induced failure is suspected and confirm with eval-harness.
4. Engineering fix: assign to owner team with SLA 3 business days for critical regressions; 10 business days for non-critical.

Postmortem and automation:
- For any regression causing customer impact or metric drop > 5% absolute, perform a formal incident review and publish a short postmortem with root cause and follow-ups.
- Add automated checks to eval-harness for the identified failure mode (e.g., add a new prompt set that captures the regression).

6) Runbook: commands and dashboards
Common commands:
- Trigger a full eval: eval-harness run --config <config.json> --output s3://redwood-evals/reports/<run_id>
- Compare models: eval-harness diff --run-a <run_id_a> --run-b <run_id_b> --out report.html
- Re-run a prompt: eval-harness replay --run-id <run_id> --prompt-index <n> --model <model_id> --save-response

Dashboards and alerts:
- Eval dashboard: grafana.redwood.internal/dashboards/evals (p50/p90/p99 latency, primary metric trend, last 30 runs)
- Canary alerts: SES notifications and Slack post to #applied-ml-evals when primary metric delta > threshold

Example triage summary template (to paste into JIRA):
- Title: Regression detected for <model_id> on <prompt_set_id>
- Primary metric drop: baseline 78.4% -> canary 72.3% (delta -6.1% abs)
- Top failing buckets: short-queries (len < 20) and safety-tagged prompts
- Reproducible: yes (eval-harness run <run_id>)
- Immediate action taken: rolled back to last-good model, traffic slashed to 10% canary
- Owner: Applied ML lead, due date: YYYY-MM-DD

Appendix: Examples and artifacts
- Example eval config: see above snippet.
- Validation script: tools/validate_prompt_set.py (run with python -m tools.validate_prompt_set <path>)
- Example quantization command: rw-quantize --model s3://models/redwood-mosaic-13b-v2 --profile q4_0 --out s3://models-quantized/redwood-mosaic-13b-v2-q4_0
